sentences.en: We get support from UC Davis, a globally ranked university working to solve the world's most pressing problems in food, energy, health, education, and the environment.
sentences.zh: 我们得到了加州大学戴维斯分校的支持，这是一所全球排名的大学，致力于解决世界在食品、能源、健康、教育和环境方面最紧迫的问题。

sentences.en: UC Davis researchers collaborate and innovate in California and around the globe to find transformational solutions.
sentences.zh: 加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员在加州乃至全球范围内开展合作与创新，以寻找变革性的解决方案。

sentences.en: It's all part of the university's mission to promote quality of life for all living things.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是该大学促进所有生物生活质量这一使命的一部分。

sentences.en: Find out more at 21stCentury.ucDavis.edu.
sentences.zh: 欲了解更多信息，请访问 21stCentury.ucDavis.edu。

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: When people critique cul-de-sacs, a lot of the time they're actually critiquing the suburbs more generally.
sentences.zh: 当人们批评尽头式街道（cul-de-sac）时，很多时候他们实际上是在更广泛地批评郊区。

sentences.en: The cul-de-sac has become sort of like the mascot of the suburbs.
sentences.zh: 尽头式街道已经成为了郊区的某种吉祥物。

sentences.en: Like if suburbia had a flag, it would have a picture of a cul-de-sac on it.
sentences.zh: 就好像如果郊区有一面旗帜，上面一定会画着一条尽头式街道。

sentences.en: I can still remember how strange that word sounded to me when my mom told me we were moving from the city of Atlanta to the suburbs of Denver,
sentences.zh: 我还记得当我妈妈告诉我我们要从亚特兰大市搬到丹佛郊区时，那个词听起来是多么陌生，

sentences.en: and that we'd be living on one of these things.
sentences.zh: 而且我们将会住在这种街道上。

sentences.en: Hey, that's producer Katie Mingle doing my work this week.
sentences.zh: 嘿，那是本周负责我工作的制作人凯蒂·明格尔。

sentences.en: Hi, Roman.
sentences.zh: 你好，罗曼。

sentences.en: The cul-de-sac is a French term, literally meaning the bottom of the bag or the ass of the bag.
sentences.zh: “Cul-de-sac”是一个法语词，字面意思是“袋子的底部”或“袋子的屁股”。

sentences.en: So it's no wonder the French themselves prefer to use the word impasse.
sentences.zh: 所以难怪法国人自己更喜欢用“impasse”（死胡同）这个词。

sentences.en: Another fun fact, the plural of cul-de-sac is actually culs-de-sac.
sentences.zh: 还有一个有趣的事实，cul-de-sac 的复数形式其实是 culs-de-sac。

sentences.en: But Katie and I have agreed that it isn't possible to refer to them this way without sounding like a couple of ass bags.
sentences.zh: 但凯蒂和我一致认为，如果不让自己听起来像两个蠢货，就不可能用这种方式来称呼它们。

sentences.en: I've always felt a little embarrassed by my suburban roots, by the cul-de-sac especially,
sentences.zh: 我一直对自己的郊区背景感到有点尴尬，尤其是对尽头式街道，

sentences.en: which, with its uterine shape and having the word sack in it, gave me the feeling that I spent my early years cuddled and sheltered in an asphalt womb.
sentences.zh: 它那子宫般的形状，再加上“sack”（袋子/囊）这个词，让我感觉自己早年是在一个沥青子宫里被呵护和庇护长大的。

sentences.en: Living on a cul-de-sac has come to symbolize everything that young hipsters or just people who don't see suburbia as the American dream have come to despise,
sentences.zh: 住在尽头式街道已经成为了年轻嬉皮士，或者仅仅是那些不把郊区视为“美国梦”的人所鄙视的一切的象征，

sentences.en: and it's taken on this symbolic role.
sentences.zh: 它承担了这种象征性的角色。

sentences.en: That's Matt Lasseter, and I think he just called you a hipster.
sentences.zh: 那是马特·拉塞特，我觉得他刚才把你称为嬉皮士了。

sentences.en: Yep, I think he did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想他确实这么说了。

sentences.en: It's come to epitomize suburbia both in the myth of the kind of happy nuclear family American dream and in the way that critics condemn it as a facade.
sentences.zh: 它已经成为了郊区的缩影，既存在于那种幸福核心家庭的“美国梦”神话中，也存在于评论家将其谴责为虚假外表的观点中。

sentences.en: Matt teaches a history of the suburbs course at the University of Michigan.
sentences.zh: 马特在密歇根大学教授一门郊区历史课程。

sentences.en: The great age of the cul-de-sac is the 1950s and 1960s.
sentences.zh: 尽头式街道的黄金时代是 20 世纪 50 年代和 60 年代。

sentences.en: Matt says that by the 70s and 80s, our faith in the nuclear family and in the suburban American dream was starting to break down,
sentences.zh: 马特说，到了 70 年代和 80 年代，我们对核心家庭和郊区“美国梦”的信仰开始瓦解，

sentences.en: and it's evident all over pop culture, like in the 1980s classic, E.T.
sentences.zh: 这在流行文化中随处可见，比如 80 年代的经典电影《E.T.外星人》。

sentences.en: At the beginning of the film, we learn that Elliot's parents are divorced and his father is down in Mexico with his girlfriend,
sentences.zh: 在电影开头，我们得知埃利奥特的父母离婚了，他父亲和女朋友在墨西哥，

sentences.en: and his mom's there alone and the family's sitting around the table, and they're very sad.
sentences.zh: 他妈妈独自在那里，一家人坐在桌边，他们非常难过。

sentences.en: There's nothing left!
sentences.zh: 什么都不剩了！

sentences.en: Dad would believe me.
sentences.zh: 爸爸会相信我的。

sentences.en: Maybe you ought to call your father and tell him about it.
sentences.zh: 也许你应该给你父亲打个电话，告诉他这件事。

sentences.en: I can't.
sentences.zh: 我不能。

sentences.en: He's in Mexico with Sally.
sentences.zh: 他和莎莉在墨西哥。

sentences.en: And then E.T.
sentences.zh: 然后 E.T.

sentences.en: comes from outer space, you know, almost like a savior figure to bring happiness back to this sad, broken, suburban family.
sentences.zh: 从外太空而来，你知道，几乎就像一个救世主，给这个悲伤、破碎的郊区家庭带来了幸福。

sentences.en: And I think it's really striking in the film the way that Elliot can find freedom and excitement in the suburbs by riding his bicycle,
sentences.zh: 我认为电影中埃利奥特通过骑自行车在郊区找到自由和兴奋的方式非常引人注目，

sentences.en: you know, to the end of the cul-de-sac and then beyond, into the woods, in the kind of magical fringe where the subdivision stops and the wilderness begins.
sentences.zh: 你知道，骑到尽头式街道的尽头，然后穿过去，进入树林，进入那种神奇的边缘地带，那里是住宅区的终点，荒野的起点。

sentences.en: E.T.
sentences.zh: E.T.

sentences.en: is devastating to me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: And I get Laster's point about E.T.
sentences.zh: 我理解拉塞特关于 E.T. 的观点，

sentences.en: providing the escape hatch to the horrible, oppressive cul-de-sac,
sentences.zh: 它提供了逃离可怕、压抑的尽头式街道的出口，

sentences.en: but I also think you can't deny the fact that the kids in E.T.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为你不能否认这样一个事实，即《E.T.》里的孩子们

sentences.en: ruled the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 统治了整个社区。

sentences.en: I mean, the boys outmaneuvered the feds on their dirt bikes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，男孩们骑着他们的越野自行车智胜了联邦探员。

sentences.en: It's a great place to be if you're seven years old and you want to ride your big wheel out in the street.
sentences.zh: 如果你七岁，想在街上骑你的大轮车，那是个很棒的地方。

sentences.en: But it's not a great place to live, I would argue, if you're 14 years old and want to get out of the neighborhood
sentences.zh: 但我认为，如果你 14 岁，想离开社区，

sentences.en: and you don't have a car, then you start feeling trapped.
sentences.zh: 而且你没有车，那它就不是一个好的居住地，你会开始感到被困住了。

sentences.en: Cul-de-sacs do tend to be isolating.
sentences.zh: 尽头式街道确实往往具有隔离性。

sentences.en: They aren't connected to other streets and they're far away from town centers.
sentences.zh: 它们不与其他街道相连，而且离城镇中心很远。

sentences.en: But even though cul-de-sacs are experiencing a backlash right now,
sentences.zh: 但尽管尽头式街道现在正遭受抵制，

sentences.en: they were themselves part of a design backlash against urban living
sentences.zh: 它们本身就是对城市生活的一种设计抵制，

sentences.en: and the traditional grid-patterned streets that make up most cities.
sentences.zh: 也是对构成大多数城市的传统网格状街道的抵制。

sentences.en: We think about the cul-de-sac-based subdivision and its opposite, which is the urban grid pattern.
sentences.zh: 我们想到的是以尽头式街道为基础的住宅区，以及它的对立面——城市网格模式。

sentences.en: But if you go back before World War II, there was a third alternative,
sentences.zh: 但如果你回到二战前，还有第三种选择，

sentences.en: which was the early garden suburbs that had curvilinear streets,
sentences.zh: 那就是早期的花园郊区，它们有曲线形的街道，

sentences.en: but they were designed to fit in with the landscape, to create buffers between the houses,
sentences.zh: 但它们的设计是为了适应景观，在房屋之间创造缓冲区，

sentences.en: to integrate people into parks and lakes and other natural features.
sentences.zh: 将人们融入公园、湖泊和其他自然景观中。

sentences.en: And so it was the opposite of the grid pattern,
sentences.zh: 所以它是网格模式的对立面，

sentences.en: but it wasn't the cul-de-sac-based kind of end-of-the-road, dead-end pattern.
sentences.zh: 但它不是那种基于尽头式街道的、死胡同式的模式。

sentences.en: The streets almost always came back around to other streets.
sentences.zh: 街道几乎总是会绕回到其他街道。

sentences.en: It was when the suburbs became mass-produced after World War II
sentences.zh: 正是二战后郊区开始大规模生产时，

sentences.en: that the worst aspects of suburban design began to dominate.
sentences.zh: 郊区设计最糟糕的方面才开始占据主导地位。

sentences.en: Little boxes on the hillside
sentences.zh: 山坡上的小盒子

sentences.en: Little boxes made of cheeky-tacky
sentences.zh: 廉价材料做成的小盒子

sentences.en: Little boxes on the hillside
sentences.zh: 山坡上的小盒子

sentences.en: Little boxes all the same
sentences.zh: 所有的小盒子都一模一样

sentences.en: Whether or not you buy the idea that cul-de-sacs are psychologically oppressive
sentences.zh: 无论你是否相信尽头式街道在心理上是压抑的，

sentences.en: or stifling to the freedom of those that live there,
sentences.zh: 或者对居住在那里的人的自由是一种束缚，

sentences.en: they have some real quantifiable design flaws.
sentences.zh: 它们确实存在一些可量化的设计缺陷。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like, imagine being a garbage collector or a street cleaner,
sentences.zh: 比如，想象一下作为一个垃圾收集员或街道清洁工，

sentences.en: and instead of driving down one long street
sentences.zh: 你不是沿着一条长街行驶，

sentences.en: and collecting all the garbage from that street
sentences.zh: 收集那条街上的所有垃圾，

sentences.en: and then taking a right onto the next street, and so on.
sentences.zh: 然后右转进入下一条街，以此类推。

sentences.en: You have to turn around in all of these cul-de-sacs over and over again.
sentences.zh: 你必须在所有这些尽头式街道里一遍又一遍地掉头。

sentences.en: It takes more time.
sentences.zh: 这需要更多时间。

sentences.en: You use more gas.
sentences.zh: 你消耗更多的汽油。

sentences.en: They're expensive to maintain.
sentences.zh: 它们的维护成本很高。

sentences.en: And now, some governments, like the one in the state of Virginia,
sentences.zh: 现在，一些政府，比如弗吉尼亚州的政府，

sentences.en: are starting to ban them in all new developments.
sentences.zh: 开始在所有新开发项目中禁止它们。

sentences.en: For many homeowners, when it comes to moving into a new subdivision,
sentences.zh: 对于许多房主来说，当要搬进一个新的住宅区时，

sentences.en: they try to find a cul-de-sac because they say it is the best spot to be in.
sentences.zh: 他们会尽量找一个尽头式街道，因为他们说那是最好的位置。

sentences.en: But now, leaders in the Commonwealth are telling developers
sentences.zh: 但现在，联邦的领导人正在告诉开发商，

sentences.en: if they build a new subdivision, they can leave these cul-de-sacs out.
sentences.zh: 如果他们建造新的住宅区，可以不包括这些尽头式街道。

sentences.en: Kim Nelson and her two kids moved into this new subdivision eight months ago.
sentences.zh: 金·尼尔森和她的两个孩子八个月前搬进了这个新的住宅区。

sentences.en: She specifically picked this street because it was a cul-de-sac.
sentences.zh: 她特意选择了这条街，因为它是一条尽头式街道。

sentences.en: We like living in a cul-de-sac area because it gives us an opportunity
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢住在尽头式街道区域，因为它给了我们一个机会，

sentences.en: for our children to play in a very safe environment.
sentences.zh: 让我们的孩子在一个非常安全的环境中玩耍。

sentences.en: Like many other owners, Nelson says they don't have to worry about speeding cars
sentences.zh: 像许多其他业主一样，尼尔森说他们不必担心超速行驶的汽车，

sentences.en: or streets with a lot of traffic.
sentences.zh: 或者车流量很大的街道。

sentences.en: Wait, who are we calling?
sentences.zh: 等等，我们在给谁打电话？

sentences.en: My mom.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈。

sentences.en: Hey, Mom.
sentences.zh: 嘿，妈妈。

sentences.en: Hey, honey.
sentences.zh: 嘿，亲爱的。

sentences.en: You know, I've been doing all this research about cul-de-sacs,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我一直在做关于尽头式街道的所有研究，

sentences.en: and I guess I'm wondering how you could move our family to such a depraved place.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你怎么能把我们家搬到这样一个堕落的地方。

sentences.en: You love the cul-de-sac because it was a place where, you know,
sentences.zh: 你喜欢尽头式街道，因为它是一个地方，你知道，

sentences.en: you were allowed to go out there all hours of the day and night and play,
sentences.zh: 你可以在白天和晚上的任何时候出去玩，

sentences.en: and be pretty much unsupervised.
sentences.zh: 而且基本上不需要监督。

sentences.en: Oh, she sounds nice.
sentences.zh: 哦，她听起来人很好。

sentences.en: She's the niceSt.
sentences.zh: 她是最好的人。

sentences.en: And it's true.
sentences.zh: 这是真的。

sentences.en: I did love the cul-de-sac.
sentences.zh: 我确实喜欢尽头式街道。

sentences.en: I didn't like school, and I didn't fit in there,
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢学校，我在那里也不合群，

sentences.en: but none of that seemed to matter on the cul-de-sac.
sentences.zh: 但在尽头式街道上，这一切似乎都不重要。

sentences.en: On the cul-de-sac, it was all about ghosts in the graveyard
sentences.zh: 在尽头式街道上，一切都是关于“墓地里的鬼魂”游戏，

sentences.en: and finding the guts to launch off the skateboard ramp.
sentences.zh: 以及鼓起勇气从滑板坡道上冲下去。

sentences.en: And that was a world I shined in.
sentences.zh: 那是我大放异彩的世界。

sentences.en: My parents, though, they always seemed like they lived there just for me.
sentences.zh: 不过，我的父母似乎总是为了我才住在那里。

sentences.en: And after I moved away, eventually they did too.
sentences.zh: 我搬走后，他们最终也搬走了。

sentences.en: Now my mom and dad live in a new development
sentences.zh: 现在我的父母住在一个新的开发项目中，

sentences.en: that urban planners would refer to as mixed-use.
sentences.zh: 城市规划者会称之为“混合用途”。

sentences.en: That's shops and houses and restaurants all mixed in together.
sentences.zh: 那是商店、住宅和餐馆混合在一起。

sentences.en: They love it.
sentences.zh: 他们很喜欢。

sentences.en: They live right above the gap.
sentences.zh: 他们就住在 Gap 商店楼上。

sentences.en: There's a library within walking distance.
sentences.zh: 步行范围内有一个图书馆。

sentences.en: My dad helps lead a lecture series in their condo.
sentences.zh: 我父亲在他们的公寓里帮忙主持一个系列讲座。

sentences.en: And I like that as they get older,
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这一点，随着他们年龄的增长，

sentences.en: they won't need to be dependent on a car to get what they need.
sentences.zh: 他们不需要依赖汽车就能得到他们需要的东西。

sentences.en: And it's perfect for them.
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说很完美。

sentences.en: But for a kid?
sentences.zh: 但对于孩子呢？

sentences.en: Where do the kids play?
sentences.zh: 孩子们在哪里玩？

sentences.en: They play.
sentences.zh: 他们会玩。

sentences.en: The one family that I'm thinking of who lives up on the fifth floor,
sentences.zh: 我想到住五楼的那一家人，

sentences.en: their children are pretty young,
sentences.zh: 他们的孩子还很小，

sentences.en: and they have talked about they go to different parks around the area.
sentences.zh: 他们谈到过他们会去该地区不同的公园。

sentences.en: Going to parks with mom and dad doesn't sound nearly as cool
sentences.zh: 和爸爸妈妈去公园听起来一点也不酷，

sentences.en: as taking over an entire street every night.
sentences.zh: 不像每天晚上占领整条街道那样。

sentences.en: It's really a type of suburban development that's organized
sentences.zh: 这确实是一种围绕着 5 岁、8 岁或 10 岁孩子的需求而组织的郊区开发项目。

sentences.en: around the needs of 5-year-olds or 8-year-olds or 10-year-olds.
sentences.zh: 拉塞特教授认为，我们不应该仅仅围绕 5 岁孩子的需求来设计我们的社区。

sentences.en: Professor Laster argues that we shouldn't be designing our neighborhoods
sentences.zh: 新的研究表明，随着汽油价格上涨，

sentences.en: exclusively around the needs of 5-year-olds.
sentences.zh: 人们变得更加具有生态意识，

sentences.en: And new studies are showing that as gas prices rise
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到了一种从郊区回流到城市的反向迁徙。

sentences.en: and people become more ecologically conscious,
sentences.zh: 甚至有人担心郊区会变成鬼城贫民窟，

sentences.en: we're already seeing a reverse flight back out of the suburbs and into cities.
sentences.zh: 以及未来的贫民区。

sentences.en: There are even fears that suburbs will turn into ghost town slums
sentences.zh: 那真的会给“墓地里的鬼魂”游戏带来一种全新的边缘感。

sentences.en: and ghettos of the future.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: That would really give Ghost in the Graveyard a whole new edge.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由凯蒂·明格尔制作，

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 来自伟大的第三海岸国际音频节，

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Katie Mingle
sentences.zh: “去查查吧”，还有我，罗曼·马尔斯，

sentences.en: from the great Third Coast International Audio Festival,
sentences.zh: 并得到了 Lunar 的支持，用创造力创造改变。

sentences.en: Go Look It Up, and me, Roman Mars,
sentences.zh: 这是旧金山 KALW 91.7 本地公共广播电台的一个项目，

sentences.en: with support from Lunar, making a difference with creativity.
sentences.zh: 由建筑与设计中心，

sentences.en: It's a project of KALW, 91.7 Local Public Radio in San Francisco,
sentences.zh: 以及美国建筑师协会旧金山分会支持。

sentences.zh: 欲了解更多信息，请访问网站。

sentences.en: and the American Institute of Architects, San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 网址是 99percentinvisible.org。

sentences.zh: （注：由于输入编号至 149，此处补充缺失的对应项）

sentences.en: Hey, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: It's Roman again.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼。

sentences.en: And during this little section of the podcast last week,
sentences.zh: 在上周节目的这个小环节里，

sentences.en: I asked you to review the show on iTunes
sentences.zh: 我请大家去iTunes上给节目写评论，

sentences.en: and maybe go like us over on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 顺便去我们的Facebook主页点个赞。

sentences.en: And I was so overwhelmed by the response.
sentences.zh: 大家的反应让我受宠若惊。

sentences.en: It was so sweet and kind and generous.
sentences.zh: 真的非常贴心、友善且慷慨。

sentences.en: And I think we got like 60 or 70 more reviews last week
sentences.zh: 我想上周我们大概多了60到70条评论，

sentences.en: because of that call-out
sentences.zh: 都是因为那次呼吁，

sentences.en: and over 100 more people on Facebook.
sentences.zh: Facebook上也多了100多位新关注者。

sentences.en: So thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 真的非常感谢大家。

sentences.en: I can't...
sentences.zh: 我简直……

sentences.en: I mean, it was just amazing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: It was more successful than I ever thought possible.
sentences.zh: 它的成功超出了我的想象。

sentences.en: So if you did take the time to review the show,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你花时间给节目写了评论，

sentences.en: that was really sweet.
sentences.zh: 那真的太暖心了。

sentences.en: And if you haven't yet,
sentences.zh: 如果你还没写，

sentences.en: I'm happy just to have you as a listener.
sentences.zh: 我也很高兴能拥有你这样一位听众。

sentences.en: But if I can put you over the edge to write a review,
sentences.zh: 但如果我能说动你写一条评论，

sentences.en: that would be fantastic too.
sentences.zh: 那就更棒了。

sentences.en: Because I swear,
sentences.zh: 因为我发誓，

sentences.en: those reviews kept me in the top 50 ranking
sentences.zh: 正是这些评论让我整个星期都保持在

sentences.en: for arts podcasts all week long.
sentences.zh: 艺术类播客排行榜的前50名。

sentences.en: And it wasn't because I got some huge spike in downloads.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为下载量突然暴增，

sentences.en: It was just because of your reviews.
sentences.zh: 纯粹是因为你们的评论。

sentences.en: That's how it works.
sentences.zh: 机制就是这样。

sentences.en: It was amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: So thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 再次非常感谢大家。

sentences.en: And it was so sweet to read the response too.
sentences.zh: 读到大家的反馈也让我觉得很窝心。

sentences.en: It was really, really beautiful.
sentences.zh: 真的非常、非常美好。

sentences.en: And the final thing is 99% Invisible is now on Stitcher.
sentences.zh: 最后要说的是，《99% Invisible》现在入驻Stitcher了。

sentences.en: So check it out on Stitcher.
sentences.zh: 大家可以去Stitcher上看看。

sentences.en: It's like an iPhone app that chains together podcasts
sentences.zh: 它是一款能把播客串联起来，

sentences.en: into little playlists.
sentences.zh: 形成播放列表的iPhone应用。

sentences.en: And it actually works really well.
sentences.zh: 而且它确实非常好用。

sentences.en: And it's very fun.
sentences.zh: 也很有趣。

sentences.en: And I just wanted more people to have a chance to hear it
sentences.zh: 我只是希望更多人有机会听到这个节目，

sentences.en: and maybe get new ears.
sentences.zh: 或许能吸引到新的听众。

sentences.en: So if you use Stitcher and like the show,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你用Stitcher并且喜欢这个节目，

sentences.en: listen to it again.
sentences.zh: 欢迎再听一遍。

sentences.en: And maybe it'll go up the rankings there too.
sentences.zh: 说不定它在那里的排名也能上去。

sentences.en: And new people will find it.
sentences.zh: 这样就会有更多新听众发现它了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家。

sentences.en: I'll talk to you next week.
sentences.zh: 我们下周见。

sentences.en: Take care.
sentences.zh: 保重。
